POST /agent/withdrawals/:id/complete now takes { provider: telebirr|mpesa, proof }. Admin processWithdrawal(approve) remains the manual override (no proof).

features.title: Agent commission on deposits (Phase 4)
features.behavior: When a deposit attributed to an agent (Telebirr or M-PESA) is credited, that agent earns a configured percentage of the deposit as commission, credited to their wallet in the SAME TypeORM transaction as the player credit (never a balance change without a ledger entry). Rate is DB-backed config depositCommissionPct (0-100). Commission is integer minor units, rounded DOWN, clamped to the deposit amount, and idempotent on the deposit reference (idempotencyKey deposit-commission:{provider}:{reference}) so a retry/duplicate submit never double-pays. features.title: Authoritative M-PESA portal receipt verification (PDF)
features.behavior: Mirrors the Telebirr receipt fetch for M-PESA. The confirmation SMS links to https://m-pesabusiness.safaricom.et/receipt/<code>, a Next.js SPA that loads its data from GET /api/receipt/getReceipt?trxNo=<code> → { responseCode, responseDescription, base64Data } where base64Data is a receipt PDF. responseCode '0' proves the code is a REAL, settled transaction (a forged SMS code returns e.g. 2032 'does not exist'). The PDF text layer is UNMASKED — full sender/receiver name + phone, settled amount, payment date (EAT), transaction type — unlike the SMS which masks the counterparty (251714***707 vs real 251714267707). New MpesaReceiptClientService (leaf module) fetches the JSON (direct or via MPESA_PORTAL_URL proxy), decodes the base64 PDF, extracts text with pdf-parse, and parses it (pure parseMpesaReceiptText). Deposit verifier: when MPESA_PORTAL_ENABLED, the portal receipt is authoritative — confirms existence+success, settled amount == SMS amount, unmasked receiver == matched agent; hard-rejects conflicts and not-found; a portal OUTAGE falls back to SMS unless MPESA_PORTAL_STRICT. Withdrawal verifier: same authoritative path — unmasked receiver == player destination, settled amount == net payout; outage BLOCKS release (admin approve is the override).

features.title: Fix repeated 'Round is running'/'Round is crashed' errors from multi-process Crash scheduler
features.behavior: Production error log showed CrashScheduler repeatedly failing to start the SAME round id every ~12s with alternating ConflictException('Round is running')/ConflictException('Round is crashed'). Root cause: CrashScheduler cached round phase/timing in process-local instance fields (activeRoundId, roundStatus, roundStartedAt, waitingStartedAt, crashPointX100), only updated by ITS OWN successful ticks. The Redis lock (CRASH_LOCK_KEY) only serializes a single tick's critical section across processes — it does not synchronize what different processes believe the current phase is. On a multi-process deployment (Phusion Passenger running >1 worker for the app), a process winning a LATER lock acquisition with stale/idle local memory would treat an already-in-flight round (created/advanced by ANOTHER process) as freshly created, arm its own local waiting-timer, and later race to start/settle a round another process already advanced — producing the observed errors indefinitely. Fixed by making CrashScheduler.runTick() re-derive phase and timing from the CrashRound DB row every tick (new CrashService.getActiveRoundEntity(), scheduler-internal only — exposes the real crashPointX100 even mid-round, unlike the public-safe getActiveRound()) instead of trusting cached fields; all local phase/timer instance fields and resetState() were removed. A ConflictException from startRound (another process won the race) is now an expected no-op, not a logged error. settleRound was already idempotent (a round already 'crashed' just returns instead of throwing) so no change needed there. ALSO hardened CrashService.abandonStaleRounds() (boot-time cleanup): it previously treated ANY non-crashed round as abandoned, which would let a newly-booting process (e.g. Passenger spinning up a new worker) wrongly refund live bets and crash a round that ANOTHER already-running process is legitimately still driving mid-round — a real financial-correctness bug, not just log noise. Now age-gated: a 'waiting' round is only abandoned past 5 minutes old, a 'running' round past 10 minutes (or with no startedAt at all) — both comfortably beyond any real round's lifetime (waitingDurationSeconds default 12s; even at maxMultiplierX100=10000 the exponential growth formula resolves in under 90s).

User confirmed intent to fix before implementation. Checked whether Bingo/Keno/Werk schedulers share this pattern: Bingo and Keno schedulers already re-derive phase from the DB every tick (no in-memory phase cache) and have no unconditional abandon-on-boot method — not affected. Werk (WerkRoundManager) intentionally keeps live round state (positions/timers) in-process under a continuously-renewed single-leader Redis lock (not per-tick acquire/release), a fundamentally different, deliberate architecture — not the same bug class, though its leader-restart cleanup (loadOrCreateActive) is itself not age-gated; flagged as a separate, lower-priority thing worth a dedicated look later, not fixed here since it wasn't in scope.

features.notes: Built via EnterPlanMode + an Explore research agent (existing agents/locations/telegram-auth code, the reverted multi-bot commit) + 4 AskUserQuestion clarifications before implementation, on branch feature/agent-area-bot. Deliberately did NOT resurrect the reverted multi-bot-one-service pattern (git 2f775f1/d6f16d5) — this agent bot is a fully independent service since its command set is nothing like the player bot's. Bot username @yaho_agent_bot is the user's literal choice, set via BotFather + TELEGRAM_AGENT_BOT_TOKEN, not hardcoded anywhere in code. Follow-up: user wanted the Mini App agent view to have full feature parity with the existing web Agent.tsx page, not a stripped-down lookalike — refactored so AreaPlayerList/PlayerDrillDown live in a new shared frontend/src/components/AgentAreaViews.tsx, wired into Agent.tsx as a third 'My Area' tab (alongside Withdrawals/Support), and pages/AgentArea.tsx's post-login phase now simply renders the real <Agent /> component instead of a separate reduced view — so web-login agents and Mini App agents see the exact same page. Also removed the redundant subtitle sentence on the Mini App login screen (phone-lock explanation), keeping just the 'Agent Panel' heading. Second follow-up: user accidentally deleted a `users` row directly via SQL for their admin account (+251936633529), which did NOT cascade-delete its auth_identities row — confirmed via code inspection that ensure-schema.ts (the schema-management script, since this project uses synchronize:false with no migrations) never creates real FK constraints, so AuthIdentity's `@ManyToOne(..., {onDelete:'CASCADE'})` is an ORM-level annotation only, never enforced at the DB level outside TypeORM's own cascade-delete calls (unused here) — leaving an orphaned password identity that both blocked login AND blocked recreating the account. User then asked to (a) restore the admin AND (b) be able to create a separate agent account on the SAME phone number, since it's a different role/permission — previously impossible because AuthIdentity's unique index is on (provider, providerUserId) alone, so one phone could only ever back a single password-login account regardless of role. Implemented multi-role-per-phone in src/users/users.service.ts: new private findLivePasswordIdentities(phone, manager?) finds ALL password identities for a phone (plain form for the first account on that phone, `${phone}#${role}` suffix for a second, different-role account — chosen to avoid needing to drop/alter the existing unique index, which ensure-schema.ts cannot do automatically) via an OR query (exact match + Like(`${phone}#%`)), cross-references each against the users table, and self-heals by deleting any identity whose userId no longer resolves to a real user (directly fixes the orphan-row bug — no manual SQL cleanup needed going forward, the app heals itself on next lookup). New private buildPasswordProviderUserId(phone, role, existingForPhone) picks the plain vs suffixed form for a NEW identity. Rewired createAgentUser (conflicts only if an existing identity for the phone already has role 'agent', not any role), ensureAdminAccount (symmetric, role 'admin'), findAgentByPhone (used by the agent bot's contact-share flow — now searches all live identities for the phone and returns the one with role 'agent'), and findBackofficeUserByCredentials (used by POST /auth/credentials — now gathers all live identities across both the normalized and raw-string phone forms, and tries the submitted password against each until one verifies via argon2, so two different accounts sharing a phone log into whichever one the password actually matches). updateAgentUser's phone-change path was deliberately left as-is (single-identity update) — out of scope, flagged as a known edge case if an agent changes their phone to one already used by a different role. Restoring +251936633529 as admin: since ensureAdminAccount now self-heals the orphaned identity automatically the next time it runs (e.g. AdminBootstrapService on app restart, if that phone is in ADMIN_BOOTSTRAP_ACCOUNTS), no manual SQL fix is required — a restart alone recreates the admin account cleanly, and an agent account can now separately be created for the same phone via createAgentUser without conflict. Fourth follow-up: even after the Telegram-link fix above, opening the Mini App via the agent bot's inline 'Open Agent Panel' button intermittently rendered the normal PLAYER Home page instead of the agent login. Root-caused (with user confirmation) to Telegram's own in-app WebView reusing a cached/already-open Mini App session tied to a persistent Chat Menu Button that @yaho_agent_bot ALSO had configured (via BotFather) pointing at the bare frontend URL — a second, independent mechanism from the inline webApp button, exactly the same class of bug diagnosed earlier for the main player bot. Rather than keep patching around Telegram's menu-button/query-param ambiguity, the user explicitly decided on the long-term fix: give the agent panel its OWN standalone frontend deployment on its own domain (agent-igames-frontend.binastech.com), so there's no bare-URL-vs-query-param split to get misconfigured in the first place. Built a new sibling Vite project, agent-frontend/, NOT a fork/rewrite — the shared UI/logic files (pages/Agent.tsx, components/AgentAreaViews.tsx, components/SupportConsole.tsx, components/Toasts.tsx, lib/api.ts, lib/models.ts, lib/utils.ts, store/useStore.ts, hooks/useSocketConnection.ts, hooks/useSupportSocket.ts, i18n/ + all 5 locale files, index.css, App.css) were copied verbatim (byte-identical, not re-derived) from frontend/src so the agent experience stays pixel- and behavior-identical to the web login's Agent page, with zero drift risk from hand-porting. Only new/authored files: package.json (trimmed to just the deps these copied files actually import — no react-router-dom/canvas-confetti/howler/telebirr-receipt, confirmed by grepping the copied files first), vite.config.ts (same manualChunks vendor-splitting as the main project, no pool/werk aliases since irrelevant here), tsconfig*.json, index.html (agent-specific title/description), main.tsx, and a new App.tsx that IS the old pages/AgentArea.tsx login flow (Telegram-initData phone resolve → phone-locked + typed-password POST /auth/credentials login → renders <Agent/>) with the ?entry=agent branching removed, since the entire domain now unambiguously means 'agent app' — always active, no query-param sniffing needed. Backend changes to support a second frontend origin: (1) src/main.ts CORS was a single ALLOWED_ORIGIN string passed straight to enableCors — hardened to split on commas into an array, since the player frontend and the new agent-frontend are different origins both calling the same API (documented in .env.example: 'https://yourdomain.com,https://agent.yourdomain.com'). (2) New TELEGRAM_AGENT_MINIAPP_URL env var (env.validation.ts + .env.example) — src/telegram/agent-bot.service.ts now opens this bare URL directly (no more `${TELEGRAM_MINIAPP_URL}?entry=agent`), completely decoupled from the player bot's TELEGRAM_MINIAPP_URL. Old path removed from the main frontend per user's explicit choice: frontend/src/pages/AgentArea.tsx deleted, and App.tsx's isAgentBotEntry query-param detection + early-return branch removed (the normal web credentials-login path to Agent.tsx, via activeTab==='agent', is untouched — that's a separate, still-valid access method for agents logging in directly via the website rather than Telegram). Verified: agent-frontend tsc+vite build clean (single new project, npm install + build), backend tsc/402 jest tests/nest build clean, main frontend tsc+build clean with the AgentArea chunk gone from the output. Third follow-up (found by the user testing the actual flow): after creating the agent account, sharing contact with @yaho_agent_bot replied 'This Telegram account is already linked to a different account' — same root class of bug as the phone-sharing case, but for provider:'telegram' instead of provider:'password'. Cause: linkTelegramIdentityToUser looked up a SINGLE provider:'telegram' identity by exact providerUserId (the raw Telegram user id) and rejected outright if it belonged to a different user — but this Telegram account already had a plain provider:'telegram' identity for the person's PLAYER account (auto-created the first time they ever opened the main player Mini App, via findOrCreateTelegramUser, which is untouched/still uses the plain id), so linking that same Telegram id to their separate agent account always conflicted. Fixed by generalizing the earlier phone-sharing helper: renamed findLivePasswordIdentities to a generic private findLiveIdentities(provider, baseId, manager?) parameterized over provider ('password' | 'telegram') — same query-both-plain-and-suffixed-forms + self-heal-orphans behavior — with findLivePasswordIdentities/findLiveTelegramIdentities as thin wrappers; renamed buildPasswordProviderUserId to buildScopedProviderUserId (now shared by both). Rewrote linkTelegramIdentityToUser(userId, input, role) to take an explicit role param (agent-bot.service.ts's only call site now passes 'agent'): refreshes in place if this Telegram id is already linked to the SAME target user; only throws ConflictException if it's linked to a DIFFERENT user who ALREADY has that SAME role (a genuine double-link); otherwise creates a new `${telegramUserId}#${role}` identity so a player-role link and an agent-role link can coexist on one Telegram account. Rewrote findAgentPhoneByTelegramId to search all live identities for the Telegram id via findLiveTelegramIdentities and match the one with role 'agent', so it still resolves correctly even when a same-account player identity exists too. Added 3 new users.service.spec.ts cases (role-suffixed identity created for a different-role user, same-role conflict still rejected, findAgentPhoneByTelegramId resolves the agent identity among multiple identities for one Telegram id) — 14 tests total for this service, 402/402 backend suite passing, tsc + nest build clean.
